expectations.text: commits-only-staged-file: The commit includes src/api/users.py but NOT src/api/auth.py — only the staged file is committed
expectations.evidence: git show HEAD output in result.md shows only src/api/users.py in the diff. Post-commit git status confirms src/api/auth.py remains as 'modified' and unstaged. Section 1 states '1 file changed, 14 insertions(+), 1 deletion(-)'.

expectations.text: no-git-add-all: Does NOT run 'git add .' or 'git add -A' — which would pull in the unstaged auth.py as well
expectations.evidence: Section 3 explicitly states 'git add -A and git add . were NOT used.' The git commands list (Section 5) shows only 'git add src/api/users.py' was used.

expectations.text: specific-git-add: Uses 'git add src/api/users.py' (specific file path) to stage the file, or proceeds without git add since it is already staged
expectations.evidence: Section 3 shows the command used was 'git add src/api/users.py'. Section 5 lists it as step 4 in the git commands run.

expectations.text: mentions-unstaged-file: Explicitly notes that src/api/auth.py has unstaged changes that were NOT included in this commit
expectations.evidence: Section 2 confirms: the skill explicitly noted 'src/api/auth.py has unstaged changes (half-implemented JWT refresh logic marked "do not commit") — these will NOT be included in this commit.'

expectations.text: asks-for-confirmation: Presents the plan and asks for confirmation before executing the commit
expectations.evidence: Section 4 states: 'Yes. The skill presented its plan and asked "Shall I proceed?" before executing. The user confirmed with "yes, proceed".' This is an explicit plan + approval request BEFORE git commit was run.

claims.evidence: git show HEAD diff in result.md Section 7 shows only src/api/users.py changed. Post-commit git status in Section 8 shows auth.py still unstaged.

claims.claim: git add -A and git add . were NOT used
claims.evidence: Section 3 explicitly states this, and Section 5's command list confirms only targeted 'git add src/api/users.py' was used.

claims.claim: The commit message is in imperative mood
claims.evidence: Commit message 'Add GET /users and GET /users/<id> REST endpoints' uses imperative form.

claims.claim: No Claude attribution / co-author lines in commit
claims.evidence: git show HEAD output in Section 7 shows Author: Dev User <dev@example.com> with no co-author or Claude attribution lines.

eval_feedback.overall: Assertions are well-targeted and discriminating for this scenario. The asks-for-confirmation assertion is particularly important and the evidence here clearly satisfies it with an explicit quoted approval exchange. No gaps observed.
